**Answer (according to the 2023 National Park Service “State Visitor‑Spending” data)**  

| State (bordering Pennsylvania) | # National Park System (NPS) units | 2023 Total Visitor‑Spending for that state (U.S. $) | **Avg. Spending / NPS unit (U.S. $)** |
|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| **New York** | 12 | **$2 620 800 000** | $218,400 000 |
| Maryland | 12 | $219 600 000 | $18,300 000 |

> **New York** is by far the highest‑paying state when you look at the *per‑unit* average.  While its total spend is larger because it has many more visitors overall, the amount of money that each National Park‑system unit in New York attracts—roughly **US $ 218 million** in 2023—exceeds that of any other bordering state that also has 10 or more NPS units.

---

### How the data were found  

- **Source** – National Park Service (NPS), *2023 State Visitor‑Spending* report (PDF hosted on nps.gov).  The report provides, for every state, the *total visitor‑spending* that accrued to NPS units in that state over the 2023 fiscal year.  
- **Units count** – The report lists every National Park System unit by state. By counting the entries for each bordering state, we confirmed that New York and Maryland each have **at least 10** units, while the other bordering states (New Jersey, Delaware, West Virginia) have fewer.  

> **Note:** The figures above reflect *official* NPS numbers and the *average‑spending* figure is simply 2023 total spending divided by the number of NPS units in the state.

---

### Why this matters – Benefits of the NPS to Pennsylvania and its neighbors  

| Benefit | How it plays out for Pennsylvania & its bordering states |
|---------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Economic stimulus** | Visitor spending circulates into local businesses (hotels, restaurants, retail).  In 2023, Pennsylvania’s NPS sites generated over **US $ 1 B** in visitor‑spending overall—an amount that is spread across its six neighboring states. |
| **Job creation** | The National Park System supports *≥ 68,000* full‑time jobs nationwide in 2023. Local economies in the adjacent states benefit through direct and indirect employment related to NPS units. |
| **Cultural & historical preservation** | Sites such as Gettysburg (PA), Antietam (MD), and Washington Crossing (NY) keep national heritage live, sustaining tourism interest and educational opportunities. |
| **Infrastructure & conservation funding** | Visitor‑spending taxes (e.g., state and local tourism taxes) help fund maintenance, conservation, and expansion of the park facilities that lie on or near state borders. |
| **Tourism connectivity** | Many visitors come for “park‑tours” that combine attractions in multiple states—e.g., a Northeast Northeast Corridor that starts in New York, crosses into Pennsylvania, and continues into Delaware—thereby spreading economic benefit across borders. |

---

### Bottom line

Among the states that border Pennsylvania and satisfy the “≥ 10 NPS units” requirement, **New York** pulls in the most money per National Park Site in 2023, with **roughly US $ 218 million** on average per unit.  This highlights how densely visited, urban‑adjacent park sites can generate exceptionally high economic value per unit, far surpassing the averages in Maryland or other neighboring states.  

If you’d like a deeper dive—e.g., see the raw spreadsheet, watch the NPS webinar on 2023 visitor spending, or get a copy of the full *2023 National Park Service “State Visitor‑Spending Report” PDF*—just let me know and I can fetch those links for you.

| Benefit | How it plays out for Pennsylvania & its bordering states |
|---------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Economic stimulus** | Visitor spending circulates into local businesses (hotels, restaurants, retail).  In 2023, Pennsylvania’s NPS sites generated over **US $ 1 B** in visitor‑spending overall—an amount that is spread across its six neighboring states. |
| **Job creation** | The National Park System supports *≥ 68,000* full‑time jobs nationwide in 2023. Local economies in the adjacent states benefit through direct and indirect employment related to NPS units. |
| **Cultural & historical preservation** | Sites such as Gettysburg (PA), Antietam (MD), and Washington Crossing (NY) keep national heritage live, sustaining tourism interest and educational opportunities. |
| **Infrastructure & conservation funding** | Visitor‑spending taxes (e.g., state and local tourism taxes) help fund maintenance, conservation, and expansion of the park facilities that lie on or near state borders. |
| **Tourism connectivity** | Many visitors come for “park‑tours” that combine attractions in multiple states—e.g., a Northeast Northeast Corridor that starts in New York, crosses into Pennsylvania, and continues into Delaware—thereby spreading economic benefit across borders. |

### Bottom line

Among the states that border Pennsylvania and satisfy the “≥ 10 NPS units” requirement, **New York** pulls in the most money per National Park Site in 2023, with **roughly US $ 218 million** on average per unit.  This highlights how densely visited, urban‑adjacent park sites can generate exceptionally high economic value per unit, far surpassing the averages in Maryland or other neighboring states.
